name: Pulse Chamber
description: Cardiac diagnostics service proposal with sculptural depth, patient cohorts and editable operational infographics.

slides.title: A referral needs a visible next step
items: The proposed service connects booking, scanning and report delivery in one accountable pathway.
The coordinator checks that the request contains the information needed for clinical review.
The booking team confirms access needs and tells the patient who to contact if plans change.
The referring team receives the report and owns communication about the next clinical step.
Proposed service workflow. Clinical prioritization follows the provider’s approved local pathway.

slides.title: Every referral has a status
items: A date and location have been agreed with the patient.
The coordinator owns the next call and records the attempt.
One mark = one referral. Synthetic cohort of 100.

slides.title: The appointment starts before arrival
items: Confirm the place and time, access requirements and the contact number for changes. The local patient leaflet supplies preparation instructions.
Conceptual illustration of an echo service.

slides.title: Four handovers, one accountable pathway
items: Clinician checks the referral and assigns the appropriate pathway.
Coordinator agrees the slot and records communication needs.
Sonographer acquires images and documents the study.
Authorized staff issue the report to the referrer.
Each handover carries an owner, a timestamp and an unresolved-actions field.

slides.title: The queue grows when arrivals exceed slots
items: Synthetic weekly referral and completed-study counts
Review demand and completed studies together. A week with fewer completions can reflect staffing, access or equipment availability.
Sample data illustrate the reporting format.

slides.title: A week has 64 planned study slots
items: Illustrative capacity plan. Slot duration and staffing require local approval. The model reserves separate time for reporting, breaks and room preparation.

slides.title: The report closes the information loop
items: Images and the study record are available to the reporting professional.
The referring clinician receives the findings through the agreed channel.
The pathway records the receiving team and unresolved follow-up actions.

slides.title: A shorter wait is a measurable aim
items: Synthetic median days from referral to appointment
The median describes the middle of the queue. Review long waits separately and break results down by the locally assigned pathway.
Example values show a possible dashboard view; they represent no measured service.

slides.title: Quality checks sit beside throughput
items: Requests containing the locally required information
Authorized reports with a recorded receiving team
Respondents who understood the next step
Synthetic audit values. Denominators describe different groups.

slides.title: Ownership prevents a referral from stalling
items: Approves the pathway and reviews exceptions. Owns clinical escalation and reporting permissions.
Owns contact attempts, access arrangements and the weekly queue review.
A weekly meeting examines open referrals, available sessions and unresolved report-delivery issues.

slides.title: The pilot tests the whole pathway
items: Confirm handovers and run sample referrals through booking and reporting.
Review every incomplete record and patient contact issue in the first sessions.
Compare access, workload and quality measures before adding sessions.
Expansion depends on locally agreed clinical and operational sign-off.

slides.title: A funded pilot with a defined decision
The next step stays visible
items: A service proposal for clinical and operational review
The pilot decision combines access measures, report-delivery records, patient feedback and staff workload.
Fictional service and synthetic data. The heart is a conceptual illustration. Clinical processes require local approval.
Reference · Leeds Teaching Hospitals, Cardiac Ultrasound. Link in template sources.
